newsitem.title: UK: Utd News sees signs of recovery at Express.
newsitem.headline: Utd News sees signs of recovery at Express.

text.p: The switch to a seven-day operation at the Express newspaper is "working very successfully", United News & Media Plc chief executive Clive Hollick told a news conference on Friday.

"We are making a fight of it in the mid-market. There are early signs that we are beginning to turn it around," Hollick said, noting a five percent increase in circulation in the first two months of the year.
Express Newspapers, owned by United, announced last September that it was shedding some 85 jobs as it put its Daily and Sunday Express national titles under one editorial team.
The Express now sells around 1.2 million copies a day, a far cry from its 1960s heyday when circulation was over the four million mark.
It plays second fiddle in the mid-market sector to the Daily Mail, which now has a circulation of over two million.
Hollick said the Express was succeeding in winning younger, family readers -- people he said might be called "soccer dads".
He said the Express was "healthily profitable" at the operating level last year although a one-off charge of 32 million pounds was taken to cover the reorganisation.
